about: Impacts with independently known impactor mass, speed and angle and a measured crater. Source IDs refer to audit/research/lit_session5/ground_truth_events.md (G01-G25), which records each source's identity, status and reading depth. Angles are elevation above the local horizontal. All lunar cases are hollow, low-speed spacecraft: outside the compact hypervelocity regime that point-source scaling was calibrated for (IMPACTS 2022: 'not ... long rod or penetrator impactors'). Session 7 added development_use (which events influenced any model choice) and morphology notes. The S-IVB crater diameters mix definitions ('roughly 30 m' vs the 29-31.9 x 33.3-38.7 m axes in G09); crater_sigma_rel 0.10 covers the difference.

events.label: Apollo 13 S-IVB
events.mass_note: from NSSDC energy and speed (G10), agent calculation
events.crater_note: 'roughly 30 m' (G11 #364); all S-IVB craters 29-31.9 x 33.3-38.7 m (G09)
events.development_use: sigma_mf = 0.10 dex was set in session 3 (experiment E1) with knowledge of the S-IVB craters; not fully independent
events.morphology_note: all S-IVB craters 29-31.9 x 33.3-38.7 m (G09): elongated at 69-79 deg elevation, so spacecraft shape, not angle, controls the planform

events.label: Apollo 16 S-IVB
events.crater_note: ~40 x 30 m elliptical with central mound (G11 #894); geometric mean used
